newsitem.title: GERMANY: Herlitz says writedown cuts 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Herlitz says writedown cuts 1996 profit.

text.p: Germany's office products group Herlitz AG said on Monday it had revised down its group 1996 net profit to three million marks from an earlier forecast of 21 million marks due to a writedown by its subsidiary Herlitz International Trading AG (HIT) on a stake in Russian paper maker AO Volga.

HIT said in a statement that its stake in AO Volga meant it had been directly affected by a "drastic" decline in the price of newsprint. HIT's group sales in 1996 fell to 495 million marks from 713 million in 1995.
HIT said it owns a stake of 33.33 percent or 18.4 million marks in Volga. The writedown has led to a "slightly negative" pre-tax profit in the HIT group.
HIT said it would now implement a plan to find a strategic partner for its Russian investment to strengthen AO Volga.
It said AO Volga was suffering from an "extremely bad home market" with low prices and sales.
HIT is majority-owned by Herlitz, an office supplies company.
